title: SIU interviews officers about man's death ; 24-year-old was pepper-sprayed by city police: [Ontario Edition]
article: The senior officer who was on scene the night Nicholas Blentzas collapsed and died after being pepper-sprayed by Toronto police has been interviewed by the province's Special Investigations Unit.

Sergeant Blair Davey, who last month was named one of two officers of the year by the city's junior board of trade, and Constable Janet Stather, a 53 Division patrol officer, showed up at SIU headquarters in Mississauga yesterday with lawyer Gary Clewley and met with civilian investigators probing the June 23 death.

Davey and Stather are the first two of five subject officers to be interviewed by the SIU since Blentzas' death, which happened suddenly after a struggle with police outside his Thorncliffe Park Dr. apart- ment.

By law, subject officers do not have to give the SIU statements because they are under criminal investigation, but it is not uncommon for police lawyers to bring them in for questioning if they feel the officers have done nothing wrong.

Four other Toronto officers, designated as witness officers, already have given statements to the SIU. They are legally obligated to co-operate with the agency, which probes all incidents where civilians are killed or seriously injured during a police operation.
SIU spokesperson Rose Hong said no arrangements have been made yet to interview the three other officers who have been designated as subject officers in the probe.
The night Blentzas died, Davey was the senior officer at the scene.

Davey, along with Detective David Tredrea, were named last month as co-winners of the officer of the year award by the Toronto Junior Board of Trade for uncovering a pedophile ring that operated out of Maple Leaf Gardens in the 1970s and '80s.
Davey and other officers from 53 Division, on Eglinton Ave. west of Yonge St., had gone to Blentzas' apartment building shortly after midnight to answer a disturbance call.
They found the 24-year-old man, who suffered from a bipolar disorder, trying to smash his way into his apartment using a fire extinguisher.

Witnesses and police say officers managed to get him to stop banging on the door and then escorted him down to the building's lobby. But once he got outside, Blentzas bolted from police and that's when the struggle began.
Officers couldn't bring Blentzas under control and pepper spray was used. He collapsed a short time later and was pronounced dead on arrival at Toronto East General Hospital.
The SIU has so far not released the autopsy findings and is awaiting a toxicology report that it hopes will help piece together why Blentzas died so quickly.
